title: CME's Duffy warns an overlooked tax risk looms over U.S. perpetual futures
summary: CME CEO Terry Duffy said a court battle over whether perpetual futures are swaps or futures could eventually affect how the IRS taxes the contracts. Independent legal experts say the issue remains unresolved.
content:
U.S. approval of perpetual futures contracts could expose traders to unexpected tax and regulatory uncertainty if the products are ultimately determined to be swaps rather than futures, an issue that has received little public attention, according to CME Group Chairman and CEO Terry Duffy.

"There's a consequence that nobody's talking about," Duffy said in an interview with CoinDesk. "There's ambiguity right there, from a tax perspective, for all U.S. participants now."

The comments come as CME continues its legal challenge against the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) over the regulator's approval of perpetual futures contracts in the U.S. Both sides await a federal court decision, and the outcome could significantly influence how the U.S. approaches the rapidly growing arena of perpetual futures. One consequence, according to Duffy, is how the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) ultimately taxes these contracts.

The dispute stems from whether perpetual futures should legally be treated as futures or swaps.

Duffy said that perps should fall under the legal definition of swaps, instead of how the CFTC categorizes them as futures, because of the periodic funding payments exchanged between long and short positions.

Unlike traditional futures, perpetual contracts never expire. Instead, traders periodically exchange funding payments intended to keep the derivative's price close to that of the underlying asset. Duffy argued that those recurring payment exchanges satisfy the statutory definition of a swap under U.S. law.

"When two parties exchange payments to each other, that is deemed a swap," he said, referring to the funding-rate mechanism used by perpetual contracts.

What Duffy sees as the main problem with this mismatched designation is that if perpetual contracts qualify as futures, many institutional traders could receive the blended tax treatment available under Section 1256 of the U.S. tax code. Under this, gains and losses are generally treated as 60% long-term and 40% short-term capital gains. If those contracts fall under swaps, they will be taxed under "ordinary" taxation. Given that the perps are newer innovations, the IRS has not issued guidance specifically addressing the tax treatment of perpetual futures.

So if the regulators or courts ultimately conclude that perpetual contracts are swaps rather than futures, market participants who have been treating them as futures for tax purposes could face uncertainty about how to report those positions to the IRS.

“So if you file your tax return and this ruling comes back, where these products that you’ve been trading and filing government tax returns as 1256 contracts [futures], when it should be ordinary, I will be curious what the IRS has to say to you about how much they think you owe them because you didn't file your tax returns properly,” Duffy said.

'Substance over form'

Legal experts, however, said that the issue is much more complex than that.

"The challenge here is that textually, by the structure, perpetual futures look a lot like a swap, but economically they perform a lot like futures," said Rustin Diehl, a tax attorney and counselor at Allegis Law and an Emeritus Fellow at Georgetown Law's Institute for International Economic Law and professor of business law at Weber State University. "It's really a substance-over-form question … function versus text."

Adding to the uncertainty, legal experts say that the definition of swaps is extremely broad.

"Basically, the statutory definition of swaps is so broad as to encompass … anything," Jason Gottlieb, partner and chair of Morrison Cohen's digital assets practice, told CoinDesk. He added that the breadth of the statutory language leaves considerable room for interpretation regarding its application to new financial products such as perpetual futures.

What it will come down to is how the court interprets it.

That's because the Supreme Court's 2024 Loper Bright decision eliminated the longstanding Chevron doctrine; federal courts now give less deference to agencies' interpretations of ambiguous statutes, meaning judges could play a larger role in deciding how existing derivatives laws apply to novel crypto products.

Tax evasion?

And it's likely to be a long, drawn-out process.

"My view is that there’s going to be a lot of litigation about it, and the Supreme Court has told courts that if there is ambiguity in the statute, they can ignore the CFTC and read the statute for themselves," Gottlieb said.

Also, rather than immediately deciding whether the products should be classified as swaps or futures, a federal judge is likely to first examine whether the regulator reasonably considered public comments and sufficiently explained its decision before approving these contracts, Diehl said.

"I think the judge is going to focus on the Administrative Procedure Act, and kind of look at the question of did the CFTC really exercise independent judgment? Were they thorough? Were they reasoned? Did they express their reasoning?" he said.

Even if the litigation ultimately clarifies whether perpetual contracts are swaps or futures, tax treatment may still require separate guidance from the IRS, which is not obligated to adopt the CFTC's interpretation of financial instruments, Diehl said.

"I think people are going to want to maybe check with the IRS and see how they should report these," said Diehl. "They [IRS] generally do agree with the CFTC's definitions of commodities historically, but there's been many times when the IRS doesn't just agree with a taxpayer submitting their tax position based on CFTC rules."

Until regulators, tax authorities, or the courts provide greater clarity, Duffy said, large institutions could face uncertainty over how to report trades involving perpetual futures.

"How would you like to be running a very large public company that trades a lot and hedges a lot, and all of a sudden you're in the news for not paying proper taxes," said Duffy.

title: IC Returns to German Football with RB Leipzig Following Haas and Tennis Deals
summary:

The deal expands IC's

content:
2026-07-30T16:26:04.363+02:00

Thursday, 30/07/2026 | 14:26 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The firm's logo will appear on first-team shirts in Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and Champions League matches.
  • Earlier this year, the company signed a marketing partnership with Mexican footballer Guillermo Ochoa.

German football club RB Leipzig has signed a two-season partnership with online trading and investment company IC, naming the firm as the sleeve partner of the men's first team.

The deal expands IC's sports sponsorship portfolio. This year, the company partnered with Mexican footballer Guillermo Ochoa after signing sponsorship agreements with the Haas Formula 1 team and Australian tennis player Alexei Popyrin as part of its international brand strategy.

The move also marks IC's return to German football. In 2021, when operating under the IC Markets brand, the broker signed sponsorship agreements with six Bundesliga clubs, including Bayer Leverkusen, FC Augsburg and VfL Bochum.

IC Becomes RB Leipzig Sleeve Partner

Under the deal, IC becomes an Exclusive Partner and RB Leipzig's Official Online Trading Partner with global category exclusivity.

The IC logo will appear on the left sleeve of the men's first-team shirts in Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and UEFA Champions League matches. The partnership also includes stadium branding through CamCarpets and LED advertising boards, as well as player activations and digital marketing campaigns.

IC provides access to cash equities and contracts for difference across multiple asset classes. The companies said the initial two-season partnership is intended to be the first step in a broader strategic relationship.

Kleanthis Rousakis, Executive Director of IC Markets (EU) Ltd, said the company was "delighted to become part of the RB Leipzig family." He said IC aims to provide clients with a "transparent, technology-driven and high-performance environment" to access international financial markets while making financial knowledge more accessible and encouraging responsible investing.

Ahead of the game 🤝

We're excited to announce @ICMarkets_EU as our new sleeve partner for all competitions and Official Online Trading Partner for the next two seasons.

Together, we'll bring innovation, ambition and exciting digital experiences to our fans, on and off the… pic.twitter.com/Oba9WGfLWP

— RB Leipzig English (@RBLeipzig_EN) July 30, 2026

IC Eyes German Growth Through Football

According to the announcement, one of the main objectives is to increase awareness of the IC brand in Germany and international markets.

The companies also plan educational content and digital initiatives focused on financial markets, economic topics and responsible investing. Planned activities include interactive campaigns, fan activations and exclusive content designed to strengthen engagement between RB Leipzig, IC and supporters.

title: The economics behind Aave proposal to ditch 6 chains that earn loose change in revenue
summary: A governance proposal would shut deployments on Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium and Aptos, and retire 50 asset markets elsewhere. Deposits on some have fallen more than 90%.
content:
Jul 30, 2026, 2:25 p.m.

3 min read

Summary

  • Aave plans to exit six low-usage blockchains, affecting about $98 million in deposits, as part of a broader cleanup of underperforming markets.
  • The six chains together account for less than 1% of Aave’s roughly $14 billion in assets and generate under $5,000 in quarterly revenue each, far below the cost of maintaining them.
  • Aave will freeze these markets to new activity and make borrowing prohibitively expensive so users unwind positions voluntarily, framing the move as both a cost-cutting and risk-reduction measure.

Aave, the largest decentralized lending protocol, is considering a proposal to abandon six of the blockchains it had expanded onto, in a cleanup affecting about $98 million in deposits. The proposal would see Aave retire “low-adoption” asset markets and 21 expired Pendle principal tokens across 11 Aave deployments, while shutting down its presence on Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium and Aptos entirely.

The arguments is based on economics. Each of the six deployments now generate less than $5,000 a quarter. Metis, Soneium and Aptos bring in under $1,000 each, according to the proposal. That does not cover the cost of running them, which includes maintaining price feeds, liquidation systems and monitoring for each market.

For context, Aave’s Ethereum mainnet deployment generates more than $142 million a year and Base about $4.7 million, while Metis produces roughly $3,000.

Deposits have collapsed across all six over six months. Soneium fell 95%, available liquidity on Aptos dropped 94%, zkSync declined 88% to about $844,000, Scroll fell 86% to roughly $2 million, Metis dropped 79%, and Sonic, the largest of the group, fell 74% to just under $8 million.

The six hold a cominbed $13 million in deposits against Aave’s roughly $14 billion across 23 chains, DefiLlama data shows, or under 1% of the protocol’s assets.

Aave’s borrowers paid about $888 million in interest over the past year, but almost all of it flows straight back out to the people who supplied the money. Aave itself kept roughly $117 million, according to DefiLlama, or about 13 cents of every dollar collected. The quarterly accounts show the same split. Of $156 million in gross revenue in the second quarter.

The numbers stop being marginal and become trivial when applied to six chains. Each generates under $5,000 a quarter in revenue, and Metis, Soneium and Aptos bring in less than $1,000 each. At Aave’s usual take, the protocol’s own share of a $5,000 quarter is a few hundred dollars. Metis, on those terms, is worth roughly the price of a dinner.

The timing is explained by the bottom line, which is falling. Gross revenue dropped from $198 million in the first quarter to $156 million in the second, a decline of a fifth. Third-quarter figures are one month old and running well below that pace, with liquidation fees the clearest casualty, down from $27 million in the second quarter to under $200,000 so far.

Existing positions would not be forcibly closed. The markets would be frozen to new deposits, borrowing and collateral use, with supply and borrowing limits cut to a single token, 99% of borrower interest routed to Aave’s treasury and a 5% base borrowing rate introduced, making it expensive enough to stay that remaining users leave on their own.

The proposal could be seen as the logical conclusion of Aave’s new direction that was set out months ago. In December, the Aave Chan Initiative proposed rolling back deployments on zkSync, Metis and Soneium as having “proven to lack product market fit,” and pushed a rule requiring any future deployment to commit to at least $2 million in annual revenue.

Aave has cast the cleanup as risk reduction as much as cost-cutting: one factor overlaps the other.

title: Tradeweb Elevates Prediction Markets Alongside AI and Tokenisation
summary:
Tradeweb reported a 9% rise in second-quarter revenue to $558.9 million as average daily volume reached a quarterly record of $3.01 trillion. 
Beyond the financial results, CEO Billy Hult used the earnings release to place the company's Kalshi partnership alongside artificial intelligence and tokeni...
content:
2026-07-30T16:25:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 30/07/2026 | 14:25 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Company's Q2 results show prediction market data joining AI and tokenisation as one of the company's strategic technology priorities.
  • The Kalshi integration remains focused on market data rather than execution, bringing event probabilities into institutional trading workflows.

Tradeweb reported a 9% rise in second-quarter revenue to $558.9 million as average daily volume reached a quarterly record of $3.01 trillion.

Beyond the financial results, CEO Billy Hult used the earnings release to place the company's Kalshi partnership alongside artificial intelligence and tokenisation as technologies shaping the next phase of institutional electronic trading.

Tradeweb now presents prediction-market data as part of the same long-term technology strategy as AI-powered execution tools, generative AI research and tokenised market infrastructure.

Kalshi Data Moves into Institutional Workflows

The Kalshi initiative goes beyond displaying a standalone market feed. Tradeweb has integrated real-time event probabilities and a dedicated pricing index into workflows that institutional clients already use for market data, pricing and risk analysis.

Clients can view probabilities linked to political, economic and financial outcomes alongside rates, credit and equity data without leaving Tradeweb. The phase described in the results centres on data rather than execution in event contracts. It does not establish prediction markets as an institutional asset class, but embeds their pricing signals in established market infrastructure.

The work builds on the first operational phase of a partnership announced earlier in 2026. That rollout introduced a dedicated Kalshi data suite, with support also announced for the American Power Index, which combines probabilities linked to control of the US presidency, House and Senate.

Talos has taken a different route by allowing market makers and trading firms to access Kalshi through existing execution and risk-management processes. The Tradeweb and Talos integrations serve different functions, but both bring prediction-market infrastructure closer to systems already used by professional firms.

AI and Tokenisation Provide the Wider Context

Tradeweb said adoption of AiEX continued to increase as clients embedded more automation in their trading workflows. TARA applies generative AI to institutional credit data, helping users turn trading information into research and market intelligence.

In July, Tradeweb completed a real-time transaction involving tokenised US Treasuries on its platform using the Canton Network. It also participated in a DTCC initiative that processed Treasury transactions using tokenised assets held at the Depository Trust Company.

The Q2 release therefore provides a strategic frame for previously announced initiatives. By presenting Kalshi data alongside AI-driven automation and tokenised settlement infrastructure, Tradeweb is positioning prediction market information as one component of its longer-term institutional technology strategy rather than solely as a retail trading product.

title: JPMorgan says fading Clarity Act odds weigh on crypto outlook
summary: The bank said deteriorating prospects for U.S. market structure legislation remove a key catalyst for digital assets, even as tokenization and institutional adoption advance.
content:
Jul 30, 2026, 2:06 p.m.

2 min read

Summary

  • JPMorgan said falling odds of the Clarity Act passing this year are a setback for crypto markets and institutional adoption.
  • The bank said the legislation would provide regulatory clarity, encouraging banks and asset managers to expand into digital assets.
  • Delays could push tokenization onto traditional financial infrastructure instead of public blockchain networks.

JPMorgan (JPM) said falling odds of the Clarity Act passing the U.S. Senate this year are a setback for crypto markets, warning that further delays could undermine one of the industry's biggest regulatory catalysts.

Prediction markets now imply just a 37% chance of the legislation passing before year-end after the Senate prioritized other bills ahead of its summer recess, the Wall Street bank noted. Negotiations remain deadlocked over ethics provisions, enforcement, DeFi, stablecoin yield and anti-money laundering rules.

“The longer the approval of the Clarity Act is postponed, the greater the threat to crypto markets from the growth of tokenization and blockchain-based applications eventually being absorbed by incumbent market infrastructure rather than accruing to public crypto networks,” analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou said in the Wednesday report.

The Clarity Act would establish clearer oversight of digital assets by dividing jurisdiction between the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), while creating a more predictable framework for crypto intermediaries, tokenization and decentralized projects.

The proposed act is widely viewed as a cornerstone for the next phase of institutional crypto adoption. By establishing clear rules for digital assets, the legislation could give banks, brokers, exchanges and asset managers greater confidence to invest, launch products and build market infrastructure, accelerating the migration of trading and liquidity to regulated U.S. venues.

JPMorgan analysts said the legislation would encourage institutional investment, boost U.S.-regulated trading and lower barriers for banks, exchanges, custodians and market makers.

Some of those trends are already emerging, the bank said, citing Citadel Securities' $400 million investment in Crypto.com and the CFTC's approval of the first U.S.-regulated perpetual crypto futures contracts.

The report cautioned, however, that parts of the current draft could deter institutional participation by allowing some tokenized securities and derivatives trading outside SEC or CFTC oversight and imposing lighter anti-money laundering requirements than those faced by traditional financial firms.

Investment bank Jefferies warned that the Clarity Act still faces significant hurdles despite clearing the Senate Banking Committee, according to a report last month.

title: Spanish Bank Banco Santander Reveals $4.3M Bitcoin Investment
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Spanish Bank Banco Santander Reveals $4.3M Bitcoin Investment
Spain's largest bank is the latest to buy Bitcoin exposure via BlackRock's IBIT ETF. 
This post Spanish Bank Banco Santander Reveals $4.3M Bitcoin Investment first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di...
content:
Spain’s largest bank, Banco Santander, has revealed a $4.3 million investment in Bitcoin. 

According to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing, the Madrid-based bank bought the exposure via BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust — a total of 129,615 shares. 

The filing is the latest example of a traditional institution seeking exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market cap. 

Over the past year, Santander’s digital bank, Openbank, has allowed customers to buy Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies and began a more friendly approach to marketing digital assets to customers. 

BlackRock’s Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) allows investors to buy exposure to Bitcoin without having to own and store the digital coin directly. 

The shares trade on a stock exchange and can be bought quickly and easily via a brokerage account. 

BlackRock’s IBIT is the most successful crypto ETF: The fund has received more inflows than any other crypto ETF, currently holding $46.9 billion in assets under management, according to its website. 

Other major institutions have bought exposure to Bitcoin via the ETFs after their 2024 approval. A large number of investors were previously put off by having to deal with things like storage and private keys but once the SEC approved a slew of ETFs in 2024, new capital entered the space. 

The crypto ETF market is already a crowded one, with popular products by top asset managers BlackRock, Fidelity, and bank Morgan Stanley already on the market.

U.S. Bitcoin funds currently manage over $83 billion in assets, according to CoinGlass data. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitchat Mesh App Defies India Cybercrime Notice After Protesters Use It During Network Restrictions
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitchat Mesh App Defies India Cybercrime Notice After Protesters Use It During Network Restrictions
The open-source Bitchat app, designed to work without internet or central servers, continued functioning and spreading peer-to-peer after authorities targeted its GitHub code.
This p...
content:
Bitchat, Jack Dorsey’s censorship-resistant, Bluetooth-enabled messaging app, has gone viral again, this time due to the Indian Government trying to get it banned from GitHub. In this latest round of authoritarian measures versus decentralized technologies, Bitchat has won. 

In July 2025, Jack Dorsey announced a new messaging application he described as a weekend project. The app, called Bitchat, was designed to work without internet access, phone numbers, user accounts, or central servers. It relied instead on Bluetooth mesh networks for local communication and the Nostr protocol for wider reach.

A year later, that same application became the subject of a formal takedown request from India’s cybercrime authorities during a period of student protests. The episode offers a clear illustration of how cypherpunk ideas—building systems that function without permission from intermediaries—continue to shape tools used in moments of political tension.

Calle, one of the main developers behind the Android version of the app, took the statements from the Indian government as a positive review of Bitchat’s effectiveness, tweeting:

“India forces GitHub to take down Bitchat

‘Bitchat enables anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification, or centralized logging of communications. 

The technical architecture of the application significantly impedes interception, attribution, and investigation by law enforcement agencies.’ – Government of India”

What Bitchat Is

Bitchat is a peer-to-peer encrypted messaging application. Devices form local mesh networks over Bluetooth, automatically discovering nearby peers and relaying messages across multiple hops. When internet connectivity is available, the app can fall back to Nostr relays. Users can join public local channels, send private end-to-end encrypted messages, and access location-based channels organized by geographic zones.

The application requires no registration and includes a panic feature that clears stored data. The code is open source, with the primary repositories hosted under the permissionlesstech organization on GitHub. The iOS version is available on the App Store; the Android version is on Google Play and distributed via GitHub releases, as well as many other app stores like Nostr’s Zapstore. Recent updates added the ability for Android devices to share the installation file directly with nearby phones over Wi-Fi or Nearby Share, letting new users join the mesh easily without the need for internet access.

Key figures associated with the project include Jack Dorsey and open-source developer Calle, known for work on Cashu ecash. Bitcoin Magazine has previously noted experimental demonstrations of offline Bitcoin-related payments moving across the same mesh. 

Earlier Deployments

Bitchat first saw significant real-world use during periods of government-restricted connectivity. In September 2025, during unrest in Nepal, the app recorded nearly 50,000 downloads from that country in a single day, according to data shared by Calle and reported by Bitcoin Magazine. Similar spikes occurred during blackouts in other regions. In January 2026, Iranian users turned to Bitchat and a localized fork during internet restrictions, as covered in Bitcoin Magazine.

These earlier cases established a pattern: when conventional mobile networks or social platforms become unreliable or restricted, tools that operate independently of those networks see rapid adoption.

The India Events

In May 2026, India’s National Eligibility Entrance Test (NEET-UG) for medical school admissions was canceled after evidence of a significant leak of the test’s questions. The controversy, involving millions of candidates, undermined the fairness of the exam and was linked to student suicides, contributing to the growth of a youth-led satirical movement known as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Protests centered on demands for accountability from Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and broader reforms to the examination system.

By mid-July, demonstrators had gathered at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and attempted marches toward Parliament. Reports indicated blackouts on mobile data or internet access in areas around the protests. On 24 July 2026, the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), issued a notice directing GitHub to restrict access to three Bitchat repositories within three hours. The notice cited the application’s ability to function during network restrictions and internet shutdowns, arguing that this architecture could impede lawful interception and attribution.

On 24 July, Dorsey posted the notice on X with the statement: “the government of India does not like technologies like bitchat and wants it taken down.” Market data from Sensor Tower, according to TechCrunch, reported across multiple outlets, showed that India accounted for approximately 85 percent of the app’s global downloads between 17 and 23 July, with more than 91,000 downloads in India over five days and daily active users exceeding 330,000 at the peak.

The GitHub repositories remained accessible in the immediate aftermath, despite the takedown attempt by the Indian government. Developers and users circulated mirrors, including on decentralized platforms such as Radicle. The application itself continued to function on devices that already had it installed, and the offline file-sharing feature reduced reliance on app stores or GitHub for further distribution. Pradhan resigned on 25 July.

Historical Context

The use of messaging tools during protests is not new, nor is Dorsey’s role in support of technologies useful during tense democratic protests. During the Arab Spring, platforms such as Twitter and Facebook were widely credited with helping coordinate demonstrations and amplify information, leading some observers to describe the events as “Twitter revolutions” or “Facebook revolutions.” Those centralized services, however, remained dependent on internet access and corporate intermediaries that could be pressured or blocked and in some cases were.

A closer technological predecessor appeared in 2014 during Hong Kong’s Umbrella Movement. Protesters downloaded FireChat, a mesh-networking application that allowed devices to communicate directly over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi without internet. The app saw hundreds of thousands of downloads and millions of chat sessions in a short period as mobile networks became congested or as users prepared for possible disruptions.

Bitchat continues this line of development, though more closely integrated with Bitcoin-associated technologies. It combines mesh networking with an open protocol (Nostr), stronger cryptographic defaults, and fully open-source code. The response to the Indian GitHub notice, which saw rapid mirroring and peer-to-peer distribution of the application itself, illustrates a further step: the tool is no longer dependent on a single company or platform for its survival; once it has been distributed, it self-replicates.

Cypherpunk Principles in Practice

In 1993, Eric Hughes published A Cypherpunk’s Manifesto. It opens with the statement: “Privacy is necessary for an open society in the electronic age.” The manifesto argues that individuals cannot rely on governments or corporations to protect privacy and that the practical response is to write and deploy code that makes surveillance and control more difficult.

Bitchat is an application of that approach to communication. It does not require user information to function; identities are purely based on cryptography. Users do not need to trust a central operator. It continues to function when conventional infrastructure is restricted. When an intermediary such as GitHub is asked to remove the source code, the popularity and the offline distribution methods of the project limited the effectiveness of the request.

This does not make the technology inherently aligned with any particular political outcome, but this is now the third time it goes viral in the context of democratic demonstrations as a solution to government-driven internet censorship. From FireChat in Hong Kong to Bitchat in Nepal, Iran, and now India, the same underlying demand appears: communication that does not disappear when the network does.  Bitchat servers that demand by giving people tools to communicate and coordinate without centralized infrastructure.

title: CoolWallet Integrates ChangeNOW as Its In-App Swap Provider
summary: Kingstown, St. Vincent & the Grenadines, 30th July 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Kingstown, St. Vincent & the Grenadines, 30th July 2026, Chainwire

Kingstown, St. Vincent & the Grenadines, July 30th, 2026, Chainwire

Hardware wallets were once primarily designed to keep private keys offline and secure.. Now, expectations have changed. People who manage their own crypto still want secure cold storage, but they also want to swap assets easily, without exporting keys, using extra apps, or relying on browser tabs. That’s why CoolWallet integrated ChangeNOW as one of the fast swap providers on the market, and the integration is the first step in a broader strategic partnership with ChangeNOW.

A few words about CoolWallet

CoolWallet has been making hardware wallets since 2014 and now has over 300,000 users, with no hacking incidents reported. Their products—CoolWallet Pro, and the NFC-based Go—combine a credit-card-sized device with the CoolWallet App, letting users manage both cold and hot storage together. Private keys are generated within the device’s secure chip and never leave it, ensuring they are never exposed to the connected mobile device. The app supports buying, staking, and swapping assets across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, EVM-compatible chains, and other supported networks.

Why it matters that CoolWallet chose ChangeNOW

Integrating a swap provider into a hardware wallet takes careful planning. The product is designed to keep keys safe and avoid sending users through untrusted channels, so the exchange feature must meet the same high standards as the device. CoolWallet has added ChangeNOW Exchange API and, for the first month after launch, ChangeNOW will be the default provider for in-app swaps.

Users don’t have to choose a provider. They just open the swap screen, pick the assets they want to trade, and confirm. The system handles the rest, and for now, ChangeNOW is the provider it uses. It’s non-custodial, requires no registration, and automatically finds rates from CEX and DEX liquidity across more than 1,500 assets and 90 networks. 

Coverage and execution carry the rest. On coverage, users move between assets and layers without leaving the app or hunting for an obscure pair. On execution, swaps settle fast and hold their rate even when liquidity shifts, since routing targets the best final output rather than the flashiest headline number.

What’s next

Together with the CoolWallet team, ChangeNOW is developing a special-edition hardware wallet for Token2049 Singapore, taking place at Marina Bay Sands on October 7–8. The limited-edition wallet will feature a custom design and include ChangeNOW as its sole in-app swap provider. Details on availability will be announced at a later date. Conference attendees will also have the opportunity to participate in an interactive activity at the ChangeNOW booth. Additional information will be shared closer to the event.

About ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW For Business is an enterprise-focused crypto super app that provides companies with secure tools to accept payments, exchange and manage digital assets, and integrate Web3 finance into their operations. Seamless integration and a wide range of supported crypto and fiat assets, alongside with SOC-2 and ISO 27001 best practices, facilitate dozens of millions of successful transactions every month for our partners operating within the FinTech, iGaming, lending and investment sectors.

title: Gold and FX Drive VT Markets to $8 Trillion H1 Trading Volume, Up 212%
summary:
VT Markets reported a

The latest figures

content:
2026-07-30T14:44:05.169+02:00

Thursday, 30/07/2026 | 12:44 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The broker reported 350K first-time traders and added 39 US stocks during the period.
  • The results follow expansion into the UAE after securing a Category Five SCA licence.

VT Markets reported a record $8 trillion in trading volume during the first six months of 2026, an increase of 212% compared with the same period a year earlier, as market volatility drove activity across foreign exchange, precious metals and equity indices.

The latest figures continue a trend of rising trading activity at the broker. In May 2025, Finance Magnates reported that VT Markets recorded a then-record monthly trading volume of $720 billion during April. Earlier that year, the company also said its annual trading volume had increased 150%, alongside growth in deposits and first-time traders.

Gold, FX Dominate VT Markets Trading

According to the broker, the first half of 2026 was marked by currency swings, changing interest rate expectations and geopolitical uncertainty, factors that influenced how traders positioned themselves across financial markets.

VT Markets said active users increased 70% compared with the second half of 2025. It also reported that 350,000 traders executed their first trade on the platform during the period.

The broker said trading activity was concentrated in gold and silver, as well as the EUR/USD and USD/JPY currency pairs. The NAS100 and DJ30 indices were also among the most actively traded instruments during the six-month period.

Broker Adds Products, Expands UAE Presence

VT Markets attributed part of the growth to product expansion and partner initiatives. During the first half, the broker added 39 US stocks to its trading offering and launched ClubÉlite, a loyalty programme for introducing broker partners.

The company said it plans to introduce additional products and platform features during the second half of 2026, including tools designed to extend trading access beyond traditional market hours.

The latest results follow the broker's expansion. Last year, VT Markets obtained a Category Five licence from the UAE's Securities and Commodities Authority, allowing it to provide financial consultation and financial analysis services in the country as it expands its presence in the Middle East.

title: A Different Way to Trade: How Copy Trading Is Opening the Markets to More Investors
summary: Trading has traditionally asked a lot of the people who do it. Reading charts, tracking economic releases, building a strategy and sticking to it under pressure are skills that usually take years to develop, and for most people, the time to develop them simply isn't there. That gap between wanting m...
content:
Trading has traditionally asked a lot of the people who do it. Reading charts, tracking economic releases, building a strategy and sticking to it under pressure are skills that usually take years to develop, and for most people, the time to develop them simply isn't there. That gap between wanting market exposure and having the hours to earn it properly is what copy trading was built to close.

The idea is straightforward. Instead of making every decision alone, a trader can browse the profiles of others who already have a track record, see how their strategies have performed over time, and choose to copy the ones that match their own goals and appetite for risk. From that point, the trades happen automatically. There's no need to sit at a screen watching every price move, because someone with the experience to do it well has already done the work of spotting and acting on opportunities.

That move, from constant participation to something closer to oversight, is what makes copy trading appealing to two quite different groups. For beginners, it lowers the barrier that usually keeps new investors out: no need to master technical analysis before getting involved. For experienced traders short on time, it offers a way to stay exposed to the markets without the daily commitment that active trading demands.

None of this depends on guesswork. Platforms built for copy trading, including OneRoyal's, give users detailed visibility into who they're following: historical performance, trading style, the markets they favour, and how consistent they've been over time. Rather than judging a trader on a single headline return figure, investors can compare how a strategy performed across different market conditions, weigh consistency against drawdown, and filter by risk level to find a match for their own appetite. That transparency is what turns copying someone's trades from a leap of faith into an informed decision, and it's what allows an investor to compare several traders side by side before committing any capital.

It's worth being clear about what copy trading isn't. Handing your trades to someone else's strategy doesn't mean handing over control of your capital. With OneRoyal, users decide who they follow and how much of their account to allocate to any one strategy. They can set the size of each copied position relative to their own balance, apply their own risk limits independently of the trader they're following, and pause or stop copying at any point. Diversifying across several traders at once is straightforward too, so no single strategy has to carry the whole portfolio. The trading itself becomes passive; the decisions around it, and the risk taken on, stay firmly in the investor's hands.

There's a learning dimension to it too, one that's easy to overlook. Watching how an experienced trader responds to a move in the market, in real time and with real capital behind it, teaches things that reading about strategy never quite manages to. For newer investors in particular, following a trader they respect can end up building the same kind of market understanding that used to only come from years of trial and error.

The arrangement works both ways. Traders with a strong track record can open their strategies up for others to follow, turning consistent performance into a following of its own. It's a structure that rewards experience without asking newer investors to acquire that experience themselves first, and it gives the whole platform something closer to a community than a simple client list.

Copy trading isn't a replacement for understanding the markets, but it does change who gets to take part in them. With OneRoyal's Copy Trading solution, investors can review trader profiles, weigh up historical performance and strategy, and choose the approach that suits their own goals, all while keeping control over their capital and how it's managed. For anyone who has wanted market exposure without the full-time commitment trading has traditionally required, that's a meaningfully different way in.

title: Solana Price Prediction: SOL Prepares for a Major Rebound as Traders Target $120–$140 Resistance Zone
summary: Solana price is testing a crucial $75 support zone as bullish divergence builds, with traders watching whether a recovery towards the $95 and $140 targets can begin.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: SOL

Solana price is testing a crucial $75 support zone as bullish divergence builds, with traders watching whether a recovery towards the $95 and $140 targets can begin.

Recent market data shows Solana price consolidating around the $75 area, a level where buyers have started to step in and defend support. At the same time, momentum indicators are beginning to shift modestly, with bullish divergence forming on lower timeframes, suggesting a potential easing in bearish momentum.

Bullish Divergence Supports Solana Price Recovery

Solana price has continued to struggle after failing to reclaim higher resistance levels, but price is now approaching an area that has previously attracted buyers.

Trader Symba highlighted a bullish divergence forming on SOL’s lower timeframe chart, showing price making lower lows while RSI begins recovering. The setup suggests selling momentum is weakening around $73.05 to $72.00 zone, although bulls still need confirmation before a larger move can begin.

The first important level sits around $75. A move back above this area would improve short-term momentum and could open the door towards the $81-$82 resistance zone.

A chart shows SOL forming bullish divergence while approaching the $75 support region. Source: Trader Symba via X

Descending Trendline Break Could Trigger Recovery

Solana price remains compressed below a major descending trendline that has controlled price action throughout the recent decline. Crypto analyst Celal Kucuker noted that a daily close above the $81-$82 region would provide the first technical confirmation that momentum is shifting back in favor of buyers on the higher time-frame.

A breakout above this trendline would be significant because it would signal that SOL is no longer trapped inside the current downtrend structure. If SOL reclaims this zone, the next target comes near $95. A stronger continuation above that level could push price towards the larger resistance area between $120 and $140.

A chart shows Solana compressing below a major descending trendline, with $81-$82 identified as the first breakout confirmation. Source: Celal Kucuker via X

Long-Term Structure Targets $140 Recovery

Gum highlighted that there is significant upside room between the current price and the $140 region, suggesting that Solana could experience a strong recovery if buyers regain control.

The weekly structure shows SOL holding above previous support while approaching a potential recovery zone. A move back above major moving averages would further strengthen the long-term outlook.

A weekly chart shows SOL trading near support with room towards the $140 resistance region. Source: gum via X

Before reaching that area, Solana price would need to reclaim several resistance levels, including:

  • $81–$82 as the first breakout confirmation zone
  • $95 as the next major resistance level
  • $120–$140 as the broader trend reversal target region

The $120–$140 region remains the major objective for a broader trend reversal.

Solana Faces 10th Straight Red Monthly Candle

Despite improving short-term signals, Solana’s higher-timeframe trend remains under pressure. Whale Factor highlighted that SOL is approaching its 10th consecutive monthly red candle, reflecting the extended weakness that has dominated price action.

A long streak of declining monthly candles shows persistent selling pressure, but it can also create conditions where sellers become exhausted and end up seeing an aggressive short squeeze.

A monthly chart shows Solana approaching its 10th straight red monthly candle after a prolonged decline. Source: Whale Factor via X

For a larger reversal to develop, SOL price needs to reclaim previous support levels and begin forming higher highs. Until then, the market remains in a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed trend change.

Solana Price Prediction: Key Levels to Watch

The immediate support for Solana price remains near $75. Holding this region would keep the bullish divergence setup active and allow buyers to challenge higher resistance.

Solana price trades at $73.66, up 0.01% in the last 24 hours. Source: Solana price via Brave New Coin

The first resistance level sits between $81 and $82, where a breakout would confirm a stronger recovery attempt. Above that, $95 becomes the next target before the larger $120-$140 resistance zone.

On the downside, losing $75 would weaken the current setup and could send SOL Solana price towards the $70-$65 support region.

Final Thoughts: Can Solana Price Recover in August?

Solana price enters August at a key technical inflection point, with price compressed near the $75 support zone after a prolonged downtrend. Early signs of bullish divergence on lower timeframes suggest selling pressure may be fading, opening the door for a potential short-term relief bounce if buyers step in.

For a recovery to develop, SOL price must hold above $75 and reclaim $81-$82, which would confirm improving momentum and target a move towards $95. However, failure to defend $75 would likely extend the correction and keep Solana trapped in its broader bearish structure, making August a decisive month for direction.

title: Platinum Price Prediction: XPT Holds Firm Above $1,600 Following Volatile Day
summary: Platinum was seen near $1,613 during late-day Wednesday trade after a tumultuous day where prices rallied and retraced.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XPT

Platinum was seen near $1,613 during late-day Wednesday trade after a tumultuous day where prices rallied and retraced.

The metal recorded gains of about 0.5 percent during displayed market feeds while sustaining prices above former session lows in the vicinity of $1,602. The intraday range ranged widely from $580 to $1,640.

Notably, the trading session opened indecisively, with platinum fluctuating between $1,590 and $1,610. Buyers returned as the session waned and provided strength until the high was seen near $1,640; selling pressure immediately followed. The price retreated slightly but stabilized in the $1,610s level to trade in the neighborhood of $1,613.

Intraday Rally Suffers Failure Near $1,640; Support Holds

Strong demand emerged when platinum reclaimed $1,600. The rally was bolstered when support broke the $1,610 level and escalated rapidly toward $1,640. The price advanced steadily before losing steam around $1,640.

However, platinum hit a wall and started to backpedal under $1,630. Sellers pressured the price further below the $1,620 territory, but it was able to cling to most gains and remains in the black over the former close.

The daily chart places strong resistance between the $1,620–$1,625 levels, but a more considerable resistance awaits in the vicinity of the $1,638–$1,640 region, as evidenced by the high posted, which precipitated the price decline to $1,613. It might take further strength in the form of buyer volume to surmount $1,620.

Daily Momentum Turning to the Upside; Slow Grind?

Additionally, the daily chart shows platinum steadily building support in the trading range where it has languished. The precious metal can be seenTrading the price in the neighborhood of $1,606 and up 0.6% on the period. The precious metal traded sideways throughout most of July from prior highs exceeding $2,000.

MACD posted a solid 7.726 on the oscillator, while the MACD line remains at minus 24.228—above a signal level at minus 31.954—indicating continued turning up in short-term momentum. The pair remains below the neutral line of 0, though it is expected to continue improving in upcoming sessions.

The Relative Strength Indicator (RSI) came in at a disappointing 46.31, with its corresponding average coming in at a similar reading of 44.71—signaling downsloping momentum as it remains below 50. Nonetheless, this reading remains notably higher than last month’s doldrums, suggesting a more gradual recovery.

Volume reached 224,160 in the period; however, trading was much greater throughout earlier sessions in 2025. Volume continues at an increased pace relative to prior months, but for price action it needs to sustain moves above the 1,620 level going forward.

Support Levels Hold As Price Chooses Recovery over Breakdown

Meanwhile, the $1,600 zone acts as immediate support now, after having resisted during the retreat of price in the later hours of trade, and the former closing price around $1,602 reinforces that barrier. Below, $1,590 stands to be monitored as potential retracement price-action levels having attracted bids during Wednesday, and a breakdown from $1,580 may open up new selling pressure toward the bottom of recent trade.

According to the TradingView chart, resistance rests at the $1,620 level for the day and then $1,630 – $1,640 higher, the levels at which selling pressure was strong. It’s not out of the question for platinum to trade within $1,600-$1,620 while consolidating on the day before heading for another assault on previous higher highs, although such a move could stall just below $1,640 or again fail.

Though the daily shows a turn to the upside, all larger-perspective returns remain on negative ground. In a broader context, returns have not gone above 16%. Looking to a closer range, price actions show 1.26% gains and a near 5% daily advance the other day.

title: 7 Crypto Risk Controls Traders in South Korea Apply
summary: It's time for some uncomfortable but helpful truths about trading: you can pick the right coin, catch a breakout, and still lose money. If this sounds a bit dramatic or unrealistic, the data shared in this article will change your mind.
content:
Skip to content

It's time for some uncomfortable but helpful truths about trading: you can pick the right coin, catch a breakout, and still lose money. If this sounds a bit dramatic or unrealistic, the data shared in this article will change your mind.

Multiple studies of retail trading activity have reached the same conclusion: most active traders lose money over time, largely because of poor risk control rather than poor market analysis. A widely cited study by researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, found that only a tiny fraction of day traders consistently earned abnormal profits after fees and costs. And when we say “tiny fraction,” we mean it: it’s less than 1% of the total population of day traders.

Crypto makes the problem worse. The market trades around the clock, volatility can spike without warning, and leverage sits one click away.

South Korean traders face another layer of complexity. The local market has historically traded at a premium to global prices (the so-called “Kimchi Premium”), local exchanges often react differently to regulatory headlines, and banking rules around fiat on-ramps create a market structure that doesn’t quite resemble the US or Europe.

That’s why it would be too simplistic to say that risk management is a defensive exercise. In reality, it’s your survival plan. So here are seven practices that deserve a permanent spot in your trading process.

1. Start With Position Sizing

A surprising number of traders spend hours analysing charts and about thirty seconds deciding how much capital to commit. That order should be reversed.

Professional traders often think in terms of portfolio risk rather than conviction. So instead of asking, “How sure am I?” ask, “How much can I afford to lose if I’m wrong?”

Here’s a simple rule to remember: risk no more than 1% to 2% of your portfolio on a single trade. Also, set the stop-loss first, and calculate position size afterward.

An example:

  • Portfolio: ₩20 million
  • Maximum risk per trade: 1% (₩200,000)
  • Stop-loss distance: 5%

Maximum position size:

₩200,000 ÷ 5% = ₩4 million.

Your trade idea may be brilliant, but the market doesn’t care. Position sizing protects you from being wrong at exactly the wrong time.

Metrics to watch

  • Percentage of portfolio at risk per trade
  • Daily value-at-risk (VaR)
  • Maximum drawdown

If you don’t know your maximum drawdown over the past year, you’re operating without one of the most important numbers in trading.

2. Build Volatility Filters Around Local News

South Korea’s crypto market responds quickly to domestic headlines. Announcements involving taxation, exchange regulation, anti-money-laundering measures, or banking partnerships can create sharp moves that don’t necessarily appear on international exchanges immediately.

All this to say, you need volatility filters.

A practical approach:

  • Reduce leverage before major regulatory announcements.
  • Cut position sizes during periods of elevated realised volatility.
  • Avoid initiating large positions immediately before scheduled policy releases.

And watch local news sources, not just English-language crypto media.

Many traders discover too late that the market already reacted to a Korean-language headline they never saw.

Metrics to watch

  • Seven-day realised volatility
  • Funding-rate spikes
  • Open interest changes
  • Sudden changes in KRW trading volume

These indicators often tell you that something unusual is happening before the headlines reach international audiences.

3. Treat Fees Like Risk

Fees rarely cause blowups. Instead, they quietly destroy performance.

A trader making dozens of transactions per week can give away a meaningful percentage of annual returns through commissions, slippage, spreads, and funding costs. This becomes particularly relevant in fast-moving markets where traders repeatedly chase momentum.

Keep a simple log:

  • Gross trading profits
  • Total fees paid
  • Net profitability

Many active traders are shocked when they discover they were technically right on direction but still lost money after costs.

You should also compare execution quality across venues. A lower commission schedule doesn’t matter much if the spread is consistently wider.

Metrics to watch

  • Average trading cost per position
  • Slippage percentage
  • Net profit after fees

4. Respect Funding Rates

Perpetual futures give traders flexibility. But they also create subtle risks that are easy to underestimate.

Funding rates can become extremely expensive during periods of market euphoria. So a highly leveraged long position may remain directionally correct and still underperform because funding payments slowly eat away at returns.

Professional traders often treat funding as a separate variable.

Questions worth asking:

  • Is this trade profitable after expected funding costs?
  • Is the funding rate signalling excessive market positioning?
  • Would spot exposure achieve the same objective more efficiently?

Metrics to watch

  • Annualised funding rate
  • Long-short ratio
  • Open interest concentration

5. Hedge With Perpetuals Instead of Selling Everything

Many traders think risk reduction means exiting entirely. And while sometimes it does, other times hedging makes more sense.

Let’s say you hold a long-term BTC position with significant unrealised gains. Selling could create tax considerations or simply remove exposure you want to keep. Short perpetual futures can offset downside risk without requiring a complete exit.

Here’s a quick process:

  1. Determine portfolio delta
  2. Calculate desired hedge ratio
  3. Open a partial short position
  4. Reassess regularly

The goal is simple: reduce damage during adverse moves.

Metrics to watch

  • Net portfolio exposure
  • Hedge ratio
  • Basis between spot and futures markets

6. Separate Trading Capital From Long-Term Custody

Exchange risk is real. History offers plenty of reminders that even large platforms can fail unexpectedly.

A practical approach is custody segmentation:

  • Trading capital stays on exchanges
  • Long-term holdings remain in self-custody
  • Stablecoin reserves remain diversified across providers and venues

When choosing an on-ramp for BTC, ETH, or XRP, think beyond fees and convenience. Some traders prefer direct ownership and self-custody, while others prefer to gain crypto exposure through CFDs. There are platforms that offer multiple ways to own crypto. For example, on Axi, traders can buy crypto for long-term investment, trade crypto CFDs or perpetual futures.

But CFDs do remove wallet management and counterparty storage considerations from the equation altogether. That’s one of the reasons so many traders opt for this strategy.

Think of it as operational risk management: a trade can recover, but an inaccessible wallet often cannot.

Metrics to watch

  • Percentage of portfolio held on exchanges
  • Counterparty concentration
  • Wallet distribution across custodians

7. Conduct Stablecoin and Exchange Due Diligence

Not all stablecoins carry the same risks. And not all exchanges manage customer assets in the same way. Besides, crypto history has shown that counterparty risk can materialise much faster than people expect.

So before committing meaningful capital, ask:

  • Are reserves independently attested?
  • Is proof of reserves available?
  • Does the exchange segregate customer funds?
  • Are banking relationships transparent?
  • Does the platform have a history of operational incidents?

Metrics to watch

  • Reserve reports
  • Withdrawal history
  • Insurance arrangements
  • Jurisdiction and licensing structure

Two Additional Rules That Experienced Traders Rarely Ignore

Keep Cash in Reserve

A portfolio that’s fully deployed has no flexibility. Maintaining a cash allocation lets you respond to dislocations instead of becoming one of the forced sellers.

Sometimes the best trade is the one you can still place after everyone else has exhausted their capital.

Review Your Trades Like a Business

Most traders keep charts, which is fine. But what’s better are records.

Track:

  • Win rate
  • Average gain versus average loss
  • Maximum drawdown
  • Trading costs
  • Performance by market regime

Patterns will appear quickly when you start measuring them.

You may discover your best trades happen only during high-volatility periods. Or perhaps your losses cluster around late-night trading sessions.

The point is, the market leaves clues. Your journal will help you find them.

Risk Management Is What Makes Longevity Possible

Crypto rewards conviction occasionally. But it rewards discipline consistently.

You cannot eliminate risk; nobody can. But you can decide how much damage a bad decision causes, how much exposure sits with counterparties, and how prepared you are when volatility inevitably returns. And that’s the real objective.

title: SBI Targets $6T On-Chain Finance Market With Canton Network Expansion and New Digital Unit
summary:
Key Takeaways: SBI Holdings has changed the name of its company SBI Security Solutions to SBI Digital Practice to favour on-chain finance activities through its initiative, Canton Network. The new
The post SBI Targets $6T On-Chain Finance Market With Canton Network Expansion and New Digital Unit app...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • SBI Holdings has changed the name of its company SBI Security Solutions to SBI Digital Practice to favour on-chain finance activities through its initiative, Canton Network.
  • The new company will provide blockchain solutions to the financial industry, including compliance and cross-border payments.
  • Canton Network already bridges over 600 institutions, enabling over $6 trillion worth of tokenized assets.

SBI Holdings’ blockchain initiatives continue to grow and be reinforced by forming a new business unit dedicated to institutional finance. The Japanese financial giant has reorganized one of its subsidiaries to speed up the adoption of the Canton Network, marking increased confidence that tokenized financial markets are making strides into using the network.

  • SBI Launches Dedicated Canton Network Business
  • Supporting Institutional Blockchain Adoption
    • From Infrastructure to Cross-Border Transactions
    • Canton Network Continues Expanding Institutional Reach

SBI Launches Dedicated Canton Network Business

SBI Holdings announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, SBI Security Solutions Co., Ltd., officially changed its name to SBI Digital Practice Co., Ltd. on June 22, 2026. Alongside the rebranding, the company introduced a new management structure centered on developing services for the Canton Network, a blockchain built specifically for regulated financial institutions.

The transfer is part of SBI’s vision of an “on-chain finance” industry which relies increasingly on blockchain-based financial products, securities and transactions instead of traditional approaches.

In contrast to public blockchains conceived for the retail consumer, Canton Network is geared toward regulated entities which need privacy versions, regulatory compliance, and interoperability, while still enjoying the advantages that DLT offers.

Read More: Gauntlet Bags $125M From SBI to Supercharge Stablecoins and Institutional On-Chain Finance

Supporting Institutional Blockchain Adoption

From Infrastructure to Cross-Border Transactions

For all participating banks, asset managers and financial firms, SBI Digital Practice will deliver the entire solution for the implementation of Canton Network. It will offer planning and development of blockchain infrastructure, construction of financial applications, implementation support, and design of transaction systems with potential for cross-border and multi-currency settlements.

Since SBI was launched, it has been actively contributing to this network, even as a Super Validator, one of the key participants in the network that validates and makes sure transactions are carried out correctly. The company has also been giving due attention to incentivize institutional participation and grow the ecosystem of the network.

The new subsidiary will likely serve as SBI’s spine to enable financial institutions to adopt blockchain technology while meeting the regulatory standards of the various jurisdictions.

Canton Network Continues Expanding Institutional Reach

Canton Network has now swiftly grown to be one of the most significant traditional finance (TFin) blockchain ecosystems. SBI claims that over 600 organizations are members of the network, such as Goldman Sachs, Royal Bank of Scotland, BNP Paribas, Franklin Templeton, Broadridge and Euroclear.

As of now, over $6 trillion of assets are managed across the blockchain, and more and more institutions are embracing tokenized financial products.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) also chose Canton Network to support digital securitization of U.S. Treasury securities in another big achievement. It also serves as an example of the ongoing integration of blockchain into the traditional financial system’s main flows.

SBI expects the demand for institutional blockchain use to keep growing as financial market participants expand their tokenization initiatives, both within the financial and investment services sectors.

The new offering does not supersede its own work on blockchain projects but rather extends SBI’s ongoing array of activations in the payments space, tokenization, stablecoins, and blockchain-based financial services.
